resources.string: Your readings and entries as one spreadsheet file in LibreView\'s layout, for your clinic, Tidepool or a spreadsheet. Only what is on this phone.
The readings and entries of the person you follow, as one spreadsheet file in LibreView\'s layout. Only what this phone has received: it is their data, not yours.
One row every 5 minutes, oldest first, with insulin, carbs and notes. The file name has only the dates, never a name. Tidepool Uploader\'s LibreView import reads it.
Your glucose in other apps: your clinic through LibreView, your own Nightscout site, Garmin watches through the xDrip+ server, apps on this phone, Health Connect, and a file for your clinic.
The glucose of the person you follow in other apps: Garmin watches through the xDrip+ server, and a file.

The xDrip+ server listens only on this phone (127.0.0.1:17580), like xDrip+ itself, so Garmin watch faces and data fields made for xDrip+ read it through Garmin Connect. While it is on, any app on this phone can read your last 24 hours of glucose from it.
Apps on this phone that read a Nightscout site (xDrip+, GlucoDataHandler, watch faces) can read your glucose and entries from here instead, without the internet. They need the API secret below.

Apps that use the current secret can\'t read your glucose anymore until you enter the new one in them.

Only apps on this phone can reach it (and devices on your home Wi-Fi while that option is on), and only with the secret. It serves the last 7 days of glucose and 30 days of entries; each reading says where it came from (this phone\'s sensor, an untested sensor, or the person you follow). It isn\'t a source for a closed loop.
The site refused the token or secret: change it
Paused: another app (%1$s) uploads to this site
Only the phone that wears the sensor uploads
Send your glucose, entries and sensor changes to your own Nightscout site, so LoopFollow, Nightguard, Nightscout reports and Home Assistant see them from anywhere.
Readings from both apps will show up on the site
Every reading, the last 30 days included
Sends readings in batches; every Nightscout has it
One request per reading; needs an access token
Sukrara stops uploading and forgets the address and the token. What is already on the site stays there.

Sukrara only uploads: it never reads your data back. Prefer an access token with only the upload permissions (Nightscout › Admin tools › Subjects) over the API secret, which can change everything on the site. Either is kept encrypted on this phone. The site needs https:// with a certificate from a public authority: a self-signed or private certificate isn\'t trusted. If another app such as Juggluco or xDrip+ uploads to the same site, turn its upload off.
Leave it empty to keep the saved one
The site refused this token or secret
Use https://: Sukrara sends your data only encrypted
Send your Libre 3 glucose and your entries to your LibreView account, the way the FreeStyle Libre 3 app does, so your clinic sees them in its reports.
LibreView asks you to sign in again (another app may have taken over the account)
From a Libre 3 connected to this phone, from the moment you switch it on
From a Libre 3 connected to this phone, since %1$s
Entries you make or change from now on; edits and deletes correct what LibreView has
Nothing more goes up until you sign in again. What LibreView already has stays there.

Use the email and password of your LibreView account (the one LibreLink or the Libre 3 app uses). Sukrara sends the password once to sign in and keeps only LibreView\'s sign-in token, encrypted on this phone. Only one device uploads for a LibreView account: if LibreLink, the Libre 3 app or Juggluco does, Sukrara asks before it takes over. Glucose goes up only from a Libre 3 that Sukrara connects to itself.
Used once to sign in, never saved
LibreView didn\'t accept this email and password
Another device uploads for this account

LibreView takes data from one device per account, today another one (LibreLink, the Libre 3 app or Juggluco). If Sukrara takes over, that device stops uploading to LibreView. Take over only if Sukrara should be the one that uploads.
Tidepool keeps your diabetes data in one place for you and your clinic. Sukrara can upload your glucose and your insulin, carbs and notes to your Tidepool account.
Tidepool keeps diabetes data in one place. If you choose to, Sukrara can upload the glucose and entries of the person you follow to a Tidepool account.
Signed out by Tidepool: sign in again
Off: nothing is uploaded from this phone
Their data goes to the account above
One every 5 minutes, the last 30 days included
Nothing more goes up until you sign in again. What Tidepool already has stays there.

Sukrara signs in with Tidepool\'s own login and keeps only the session, never your password. If Tidepool already gets your Libre data through LibreView, turn glucose off here, or each reading shows up twice.
Used once to sign in, never saved
Tidepool didn\'t accept this email and password

Apps on this phone that take glucose from xDrip+, LibreLink or Juggluco broadcasts (AndroidAPS, GlucoDataHandler, watch apps) can get each new reading from this phone\'s Libre 3. Only the apps you switch on get it.

Install the app (for example AndroidAPS or GlucoDataHandler) and come back
%1$s · this app changed since you allowed it (another signature), so nothing is sent · Tap to allow it again

Only the Libre 3 this phone reads itself is sent, at most once a minute, and never LO / HI, old readings or a followed person\'s data. Each app gets one format (xDrip+ first, then LibreLink, then Juggluco), so it never gets a reading twice. A closed loop may dose insulin from these readings: allow only the apps you use.
Your glucose in Health Connect, where health and fitness apps you allow can read it. Only readings from this phone\'s own sensor go in, once a minute.
Health Connect doesn\'t allow writing now · nothing is written until you allow it again

Allow Sukrara to write blood glucose
Nothing is written on a follower\'s phone: Health Connect holds this phone owner\'s own health records, and the glucose here is the person you follow.
Health Connect isn\'t available on this phone (it may be turned off in Android settings).

When you turn it on, the last 30 days go in first. Each minute is one record, so nothing is written twice. LO and HI readings have no number and are left out. Turning it off stops writing; delete what was written in Health Connect.
AndroidAPS may get each reading twice
xDrip+ and GlucoDataHandler can pass readings on to AndroidAPS. If one of them does, switch AndroidAPS off here or turn their forwarding off, so AndroidAPS gets each reading once.

Permissions › Nearby devices › Allow. Keep it allowed: the sensor connection needs it too. To stop, use the switch above.

Any device on this Wi-Fi (computers, TVs, guests\' phones) can read your glucose, doses and notes with the API secret. The connection isn\'t encrypted: someone on the same Wi-Fi can see the secret when an app sends it. It works only on the Wi-Fi you turn it on in, and never on Wi-Fi without a password.
Open the API to your home Wi-Fi?
Not turned on: it works only while the phone is on a home Wi-Fi with a password

%1$s (%2$s) is signed with a different key than when you allowed it. That happens when it was reinstalled from another source, and it can also be a different app using the same name. Allow it again only if you installed it yourself from a source you trust: an app like AndroidAPS may dose insulin from these readings.
